All kinds of marine plants, from apex predators down to the plankton at the base of the food chain, ingest plastics. These can cause severe harm to the animals, affecting food uptake by creating a false sense of satiation or blockages in digestive systems, as well as leading to internal damages

. Several studies in the laboratory experiments have shown reduced growth in fish when their food is contaminated by higher amounts of microplastics; (Naidoo and Glassom, 2019) while at the other extreme a single plastic drinking straw in its digestive system likely caused the death of a whale shark in Thailand (Haetrakulet al., 2009). Plastic pollution is one of several manmade threats

including ocean warming, overharvesting, ocean acidification, eutrophication, deoxygenation, shipping and underwater noise, invasive species, habitat destruction and fragmentation, as well as other forms of chemical pollution.
